### AccountKind

`personal`: one person's own account, made at their first sign-in; what they create is theirs alone unless they move it. `organisation`: an account people create or join, where sandboxes and snapshots are shared.

One of: `"personal"` or `"organisation"`.

### ApiKeyPreset

A named set of scopes. `read-only`: the `:read` scopes. `agent`: what a coding agent needs to make and drive its own sandboxes, everything but `sandboxes:delete` and the account and host scopes. `ci`: `agent` plus `sandboxes:delete`. `admin`: every scope but `hosts:admin`.

One of: `"read-only"` or `"agent"` or `"ci"` or `"admin"`.

### ApiKeyScope

What a key may do. `sandboxes:read`: list and inspect sandboxes, their usage and events. `sandboxes:write`: create, change, start, stop, pause, resume, fork and recover. `sandboxes:delete`: delete for good. `exec`: run commands. `files`: read and write files. `access`: SSH, desktop, browser and public ports. `snapshots:read`, `snapshots:write`: snapshots and saved snapshots. `account:read`: the account, its members, keys, environments, templates and sandboxes' egress. `account:admin`: members, keys, webhooks, telemetry, the proxy, environments, templates and sandboxes' grants. `hosts:admin`: the deployment's hosts and template bases, for a super-admin's key only.

One of: `"sandboxes:read"` or `"sandboxes:write"` or `"sandboxes:delete"` or `"exec"` or `"files"` or `"access"` or `"snapshots:read"` or `"snapshots:write"` or `"account:read"` or `"account:admin"` or `"hosts:admin"`.

### ApproveDeviceLoginBody

What the device gets. A sign-in that asked for a personal token is approved with `personal: true`, and gets one acting as the approver, in `accounts` or all of theirs, capped by `preset` when given; `account` is ignored. Any other gets an API key in the approver's personal account unless `account` names an organisation, which needs admin or owner there; without `preset`, every scope the approver may grant there, `hosts:admin` included for a super-admin.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account` | string | no | The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`. |
| `preset` | [ApiKeyPreset](/api/reference/types/#apikeypreset) | no |  |
| `personal` | boolean | no | True to approve a sign-in that asked for a personal token, which then acts as the approver in `accounts` or all of theirs. Required for one: an approval without it, as from a console that showed an API key, is refused. |
| `accounts` | string[] | no | For a personal token: only these accounts. Absent: every account of the approver's. |
| `expiresInDays` | integer | no | Default 90. It stops working after it. A personal token lasts at most 366. (minimum 1, maximum 3650) |

### BucketCredentials

Write-only: kept encrypted, given only to the host of a sandbox that mounts the bucket, never answered.

One of: [BucketAccessKey](/api/reference/types/#bucketaccesskey) or [BucketServiceAccountKey](/api/reference/types/#bucketserviceaccountkey).

### BucketMountSource

An object-store prefix, through a bucket source the account holds. The host reads objects as they are opened; the bucket source's credentials stay on the host, never in the sandbox.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"bucket"` | yes |  |
| `bucketSourceId` | string | yes | A bucket source of the sandbox's account, such as `bks_4kq9x2mt`. |
| `prefix` | string | yes | The objects under this key prefix, such as `org/42/skills/`; empty for the whole bucket. (at most 1024 characters) |
| `refreshTtlSeconds` | integer | no | How long the host trusts its listing of the prefix before it looks again, so objects added later appear: it looks when the sandbox next uses the mount after that, and that use still sees the old listing. 0: never look again. Default: the host's (60). To have the sandbox see a change before it next uses the mount, call `refreshSandboxMounts`. (minimum 0, maximum 86400) |

### BucketProvider

`s3`: Amazon S3 or an S3-compatible store (with `endpoint`). `gcs`: Google Cloud Storage.

One of: `"s3"` or `"gcs"`.

### CommandNeedsMicrovm

In an isolate: the command failed because it ran something an isolate doesn't have. Upgrade the sandbox (`upgradeSandbox`) and run it again, or give the sandbox `autoUpgrade`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | string | yes | What it ran that an isolate doesn't have, such as `tar`. |
| `reason` | string | yes | Why, in one sentence. |
| `inferred` | boolean | no | Read by Kantel from the shell's answer (exit 127 and its message), not said by the isolate's runtime: a hint only. A command can print that text itself, so `autoUpgrade` never acts on it. |

### CommandState

One of: `"running"` or `"exited"` or `"killed"` or `"timed_out"`.

### CommandTermination

In an isolate: its runtime stopped the command for using too much CPU time (`cpu`), memory (`memory`) or wall time (`wall`).

One of: `"cpu"` or `"memory"` or `"wall"`.

### Cost

What a sandbox costs at the deployment's rates. A self-hosted install's rates are 0 unless its operator sets them.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `currency` | string | yes | ISO 4217, such as `USD`. |
| `total` | number | yes | What it has cost so far, in `currency`. |
| `ratePerHour` | number | yes | What an hour of running costs at its size, in `currency`. |

### CreateSandboxBody

Every field is optional: `{}` makes a running isolate in the caller's account.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `account` | string | no | The account to act in: the caller's personal account (the default for a person) or an organisation they belong to. An API key always acts in its own account, and naming another is `forbidden`. |
| `name` | string | no | Default: a generated name, such as `brave-otter`. (at most 63 characters) |
| `type` | [SandboxType](/api/reference/types/#sandboxtype) | no |  |
| `size` | [SandboxSizeName](/api/reference/types/#sandboxsizename) | no |  |
| `resources` | [SandboxShapeInput](/api/reference/types/#sandboxshapeinput) | no |  |
| `image` | string | no | A microVM's base image. Default: the deployment's. |
| `from` | string | no | Start from this snapshot: a snapshot's ID or a saved snapshot's name in the account. |
| `autoStopMinutes` | integer or null | no | Default 60. `null`: never stop by itself. |
| `idleStopMinutes` | integer or null | no | Stop it once it has gone this long without use (`idle-stop`), whatever its auto-stop says; with `autoStopMinutes: null`, it runs while it is used. Default `null`: no idle stop. See the sandbox's `idleStopMinutes` for what counts as use. |
| `visibility` | [SandboxVisibility](/api/reference/types/#sandboxvisibility) | no |  |
| `labels` | Record&lt;string, string&gt; | no |  |
| `env` | Record&lt;string, string&gt; | no | Environment variables every command sees, after its environments'. Not secrets: they are shown to anyone who may exec. Kantel's own names (`KANTEL_*`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, in any case) are refused. |
| `environment` | string | no | Start with this environment, an environment's ID or name in the account: its plain variables, a placeholder for each protected one, its secret files and repositories, and its grants. `env` may not name one of its protected variables. Give `environments` for more than one. |
| `environments` | string[] | no | Start with these environments, each an ID or name in the account, in order: as `environment` gives one, and where two set the same variable, file or repository path, the later one wins. Not with `environment`. (at most 10 items) |
| `template` | string | no | Make a microVM from this template, a template's ID or name in the account (experimental, `KANTEL_TEMPLATES`): from its newest built snapshot when one is ready, else by booting its image and running its setup. A Dockerfile or image reference boots only once its current version's image is built (`unavailable` until then), on the host that built it. Its variables go under the environment's and `env`, its grants with the sandbox's own, and with `size` left out its resources are the machine's, exactly (`resources`), named by the smallest size with them. Not with `from` or `image`. A template with setup needs a key with `exec` too: a host may boot it fresh whatever its snapshot, running the setup with the sandbox's variables. |
| `stickyDisks` | [SandboxStickyDiskInput](/api/reference/types/#sandboxstickydiskinput)[] | no | Sticky disks to attach (experimental, a microVM's): each a copy of the newest version its host has, mounted at its path. Needs a host that runs them. (at most 2 items) |
| `hostLabels` | Record&lt;string, string&gt; | no | Place it only on a host with each label, such as `{ site: "home" }`. |
| `host` | string | no | Place it on this host, a host's ID or name: one of the account's own hosts, or for a super-admin a shared one (any other is `not_found`). It stays on that host, as every sandbox stays where it was placed. `unavailable` (`host_unavailable`) when that host is offline, draining, doesn't run the type, lacks a `hostLabels` label or (for a create from a snapshot) doesn't hold the snapshot. Default: whichever host placement picks. |
| `mounts` | [Mount](/api/reference/types/#mount)[] | no | Files from outside the sandbox, read-only inside it: at most 16, at paths that don't overlap. A bundle or bucket source it names must be the account's. microVMs only: an isolate is refused (`not_supported`). A host that can't mount a source marks that mount `failed`, and the sandbox runs without it. A fork keeps its source's mounts. Experimental: `not_supported` unless the deployment has turned mounts on (`KANTEL_MOUNTS=experimental`). (at most 16 items) |
| `autoUpgrade` | boolean | no | For an isolate: when its runtime says a command needs something an isolate lacks (a program such as `tar`, a package manager, Docker), upgrade it to a microVM (`upgradeSandbox`, the deployment's default size) and run the whole command again there, once: what it did before the step that failed is done again. Setting it needs `sandboxes:write`, and with it any caller that may run commands in the sandbox (`exec`) may cause the upgrade. Only a `needsMicrovm` the runtime says counts, never one read from the command's output (`inferred`). Default false: the command answers `needsMicrovm` and the isolate stays as it is. |
| `wait` | boolean | no | Answer once it is `running` (or `error`) rather than as soon as it is placed. |

### EventType

`sandbox.created`: made, before it runs. `sandbox.running`: it runs commands now, after a create, resume, fork or recovery. `sandbox.stopped`, `sandbox.paused`: it stopped (by a call, its auto-stop or its idle stop), or paused. `sandbox.error`: it entered `error`. `sandbox.degraded`, `sandbox.recovered`: its host lost and regained it; `sandbox.degraded` also when its environment's secret file or repository couldn't be set up (its reason says which), which leaves it running, and when its guest agent stops answering (its `health` `unresponsive`), with `sandbox.recovered` once it answers again. `sandbox.environments_changed`: an environment was attached to it or detached from it (`data.attached` or `data.detached`, and `data.environmentIds`, in order). `sandbox.oom_kill`: a microVM ran out of memory and its kernel killed processes (`data.oomKills` of them since its last reading); it keeps running. `sandbox.upgraded`: an isolate became a microVM with the same ID (`upgradeSandbox`, or its `autoUpgrade`): `data.from` and `data.to` the types, `data.previousState`, `data.path` (`host` when its own host made the microVM, `control-plane` when its files were moved to another host), `data.files`, `data.bytes` and `data.durationMs`. `sandbox.deleted`: erased. `snapshot.saved`, `snapshot.deleted`: a saved snapshot was made or deleted.

One of: `"sandbox.created"` or `"sandbox.running"` or `"sandbox.stopped"` or `"sandbox.paused"` or `"sandbox.error"` or `"sandbox.degraded"` or `"sandbox.recovered"` or `"sandbox.environments_changed"` or `"sandbox.oom_kill"` or `"sandbox.upgraded"` or `"sandbox.deleted"` or `"snapshot.saved"` or `"snapshot.deleted"`.

### GithubRunnerPool

Runners of one shape, picked by a `runs-on` label.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | string | yes | The `runs-on` label that picks this pool, such as `kantel-8vcpu`. Lower case. |
| `template` | string | yes | The template each runner's microVM is made from, an ID or name in the account. Its image must have the GitHub Actions runner at `runnerCommand`'s path. |
| `resources` | [GithubRunnerResources](/api/reference/types/#githubrunnerresources) | yes |  |
| `hostLabels` | Record&lt;string, string&gt; | no | Run only on hosts with each of these labels. |
| `environments` | string[] | no | Environments each runner starts with, IDs or names in the account, such as one holding a cache token. (at most 10 items) |
| `maxRunners` | integer | no | The most runners the pool has at once, starting or running. Default 20. (minimum 1, maximum 500) |
| `timeoutMinutes` | integer | no | How long a runner may live, start to finish, before it is deleted whatever it is doing. Default 360. (minimum 5, maximum 4320) |
| `stickyDisks` | [GithubRunnerStickyDisk](/api/reference/types/#githubrunnerstickydisk)[] | no | Sticky disks each runner gets a copy of (`KANTEL_STICKY_DISKS`). (at most 2 items) |
| `runnerCommand` | string | no | The shell command that starts the runner, run as the sandbox's default user (`user`, not root) with the just-in-time configuration in `KANTEL_RUNNER_JITCONFIG` and the egress proxy's variables. Default `sudo -n --preserve-env=HTTP_PROXY,HTTPS_PROXY,NO_PROXY,http_proxy,https_proxy,no_proxy,NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY runuser -u runner -- /home/runner/actions-runner/run.sh --jitconfig "$KANTEL_RUNNER_JITCONFIG"`. (at most 4096 characters) |
| `repositories` | string[] | no | Only jobs of these repositories (`owner/name`) get this pool's runners; a job of any other that asks for its label is `ignored`. Absent: any the integration serves. It keeps one repository's jobs off another's runners only with `scope: repository`: a runner registered on the organization may take any job with its labels. (at most 500 items) |

### GithubRunnerStickyCommit

When a runner's copy becomes the disk's next version: after a job that succeeded on that runner, on a run GitHub says is a scheduled run of one of `branches` in the job's own repository. Push and manual runs don't commit for now: GitHub gives a tag's run the tag's name as its branch, and says nothing that tells them apart. Pull requests never commit.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `branches` | string[] | yes | Branches whose successful scheduled jobs commit the runner's copy: the repository's default branch, such as `main`. (at most 20 items) |
| `beforeCommit` | string | no | A shell command run as root in the runner before its copy is committed, such as one that prunes the cache and stops Docker. A commit is skipped when it fails. (at most 4096 characters) |

### HostDiskUsage

What takes the space on a host's disk, as the host measured it last (every few minutes), counting only files on the filesystem that holds the host's files. Each file counts once, in the first of these it is in: bundles, images, templates, sandboxes, snapshots. Memory a stop's snapshot shares with its sandbox counts for the sandbox. Snapshots are split into saved and automatic by Kantel's own records, not by the host.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `totalBytes` | integer | yes | The size of the filesystem that holds the host's files. (minimum 0) |
| `usedBytes` | integer | yes | What is used on it, by anything. (minimum 0) |
| `savedSnapshotsBytes` | integer | yes | Saved snapshots: of the snapshot files counted here, those every account's saved snapshots on the host hold, each file once. (minimum 0) |
| `automaticSnapshotsBytes` | integer | yes | The rest of the host's snapshots: automatic ones, and any Kantel has no record of. (minimum 0) |
| `sandboxesBytes` | integer | yes | Sandboxes' own disks, and their memory while they're stopped. (minimum 0) |
| `imagesBytes` | integer | yes | Base images: the guest kernel and root filesystems, and templates' root filesystems. (minimum 0) |
| `templatesBytes` | integer | yes | Template snapshots, which new sandboxes start from. (minimum 0) |
| `bundlesBytes` | integer | yes | The cache of bundle images that sandboxes mount. (minimum 0) |
| `otherBytes` | integer | yes | The rest of the used space: the operating system, logs and other programs. (minimum 0) |
| `measuredAt` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |

### HostMemory

A host's memory, in MiB, as it last reported it (every heartbeat).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `"reserved"` or `"used"` | yes | How the host admits microVMs' memory. `reserved`: by what they were given, up to `maxRatio` times `capacityMiB`. `used` (memory over-commit, experimental): by `committedMiB`, what they use and may soon use, within what the machine has available and up to `maxRatio` times `capacityMiB` given. |
| `state` | `"ok"` or `"tight"` or `"refusing"` or `"critical"` | yes | How short of memory the host is. `tight`: it reclaims guests' page cache. `refusing`: it refuses new sandboxes. `critical`: it ends the largest process in the guest holding the most memory. |
| `totalMiB` | integer | yes | The machine's memory, or the limit of the control group kantel-host runs in. (minimum 0) |
| `reserveMiB` | integer | yes | What is kept for the host's own processes and never given to sandboxes. (minimum 0) |
| `capacityMiB` | integer | yes | `totalMiB` less `reserveMiB`. (minimum 0) |
| `reservedMiB` | integer | yes | What the host's sandboxes were given. (minimum 0) |
| `committedMiB` | integer | yes | What its microVMs count for: each its peak of the last minutes plus headroom, at most its size. (minimum 0) |
| `guestUsedMiB` | integer | yes | What its microVMs' guests say they use, page cache aside. (minimum 0) |
| `residentMiB` | integer | yes | What its microVMs hold of the machine's memory, their guests' page cache included. (minimum 0) |
| `availableMiB` | integer | yes | What the machine has available now (MemAvailable). (minimum 0) |
| `swapUsedMiB` | integer | yes | Swap in use on the machine. (minimum 0) |
| `pressureSome` | number | yes | Memory pressure: the share of the last 10 seconds some task waited on memory. (minimum 0, maximum 100) |
| `pressureFull` | number | yes | The share of the last 10 seconds every task waited on memory. (minimum 0, maximum 100) |
| `maxRatio` | number | yes | The most sandboxes may be given, as a multiple of `capacityMiB`. (minimum 0) |
| `measuredAt` | integer | no | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |

### MemberRole

`member`: uses the organisation's shared sandboxes and snapshots and makes their own. `admin`: also manages members, API keys, webhooks, telemetry and the proxy. `owner`: also renames or deletes the organisation. A personal account's person is its `owner`.

One of: `"member"` or `"admin"` or `"owner"`.

### MicrovmShapes

Absent when no host the account may use runs microVMs. `diskGb` is the disk a microVM may ask for (`resources.diskGb`), whatever its vCPUs and memory: within the hosts' limits and the free disk they last reported, its `default` the default preset's. A sandbox no host has the free disk for now goes to `error` with `placementReason` `insufficient_capacity`. `diskGb` is absent when no host takes a disk off its presets, or none has the free disk for its least.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vcpus` | [ShapeRange](/api/reference/types/#shaperange) | yes |  |
| `memoryMb` | [ShapeRange](/api/reference/types/#shaperange) | yes |  |
| `memoryMbPerVcpu` | object | yes | Memory follows vCPUs: each vCPU has at least `min` and at most `max` MB. |

### PersonalTokenPolicy

Whether members' personal access tokens (`kpt_…`) may act in the organisation. `blocked`: a call made with one is `forbidden` there, and members use the console or one of the organisation's API keys. Always `allowed` in a personal account. Absent from a gateway before it: `allowed`.

One of: `"allowed"` or `"blocked"`.

### PlacementReason

Why a sandbox couldn't be placed on a host. `no_host`: no host it may use is connected. `no_host_for_type`: none runs its type. `no_host_with_labels`: none has every label in `hostLabels`. `no_host_offers_size`: none offers its size or can make its resources. `no_host_enforces_egress`: none that could take it enforces egress grants or protected variables. `no_host_for_template`: none that could take it runs templates, or builds the template's custom image. `insufficient_capacity`: hosts match but none has the memory or disk free now; retry later. `host_unavailable`: the host its disk or snapshot is on can't take it now (offline, draining or not one it may use, or gone during the boot). `account_limit`: the account runs as many sandboxes as it may.

One of: `"no_host"` or `"no_host_for_type"` or `"no_host_with_labels"` or `"no_host_offers_size"` or `"no_host_enforces_egress"` or `"no_host_for_template"` or `"insufficient_capacity"` or `"host_unavailable"` or `"account_limit"`.

### SandboxHealth

`degraded`: the machine is up but its host can't fully reach it; it keeps running. `unresponsive`: it is running, but its guest agent has stopped answering its host (out of memory, say; its `reason` says why), so its commands and files are refused at once (`sandbox_unresponsive`) rather than left to hang. Recover it (a restart that keeps its disk), or stop and start it; it is `ok` again by itself should its agent answer first.

One of: `"ok"` or `"degraded"` or `"unresponsive"`.

### SandboxNotRunning

The `details` of the `conflict` (409) a call that needs a running sandbox (commands, files, ports, file URLs, archives) answers when the sandbox isn't running. A call made while it is starting waits for it, up to 60 seconds, before it answers `sandbox_starting`. Kantel never resumes a stopped sandbox for such a call.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | [SandboxNotRunningCode](/api/reference/types/#sandboxnotrunningcode) | yes |  |
| `sandboxId` | string | yes |  |
| `state` | [SandboxState](/api/reference/types/#sandboxstate) | yes |  |
| `stopReason` | string | no | Why it stopped, paused or failed, where Kantel recorded it (the sandbox's `reason`): `auto-stop` when its auto-stop time came, `idle-stop` when it went `idleStopMinutes` without use, a rule's reason when Kantel stopped it, or what failed. A stop someone asked for has none. Not `details.reason`, which is a placement's. |
| `hint` | string | yes | What to do, in words, such as `Resume it with kantel resume sbx_4kq9x2mt or POST /v1/sandboxes/sbx_4kq9x2mt/resume, then try again`. |

### SandboxNotRunningCode

Why a call that needs a running sandbox was refused. `sandbox_starting`: it was still starting when the call's wait for it ran out; send the call again. `sandbox_stopping`, `sandbox_stopped`, `sandbox_paused`, `sandbox_error`: resume it (`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/resume`), then send the call again. `sandbox_deleting`: it is being deleted. `sandbox_unresponsive`: it is running, but its guest agent doesn't answer (its `health` is `unresponsive`; `stopReason` says why, such as out of memory): recover it (`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/recover`, a restart that keeps its disk), or wait for the agent to answer again.

One of: `"sandbox_starting"` or `"sandbox_stopping"` or `"sandbox_stopped"` or `"sandbox_paused"` or `"sandbox_error"` or `"sandbox_deleting"` or `"sandbox_unresponsive"`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `memUsedBytes` | integer | yes | Memory in use at `at`. For a microVM, what its guest counts as used (total less available, page cache not counted), so it falls when the guest frees memory; from a host or VM that can't report that, the memory the VM holds on its host, which stays near its high point. For an isolate, its share of its account's runtime. (minimum 0) |
| `diskUsedBytes` | integer | no | A microVM's own disk in use at `at`, as its guest counts it (df's used). Absent for an isolate, and where the host or the guest's agent doesn't send it. (minimum 0) |
| `ioPressure` | number | no | The share of the interval ending at `at` in which at least one of a microVM's tasks waited on IO (its guest kernel's IO pressure, `some`). Absent where the guest has no pressure figures. (minimum 0, maximum 1) |
| `oomKills` | integer | no | How many processes a microVM's kernel had killed for memory since it booted, at `at`. Absent where its guest's agent doesn't send it or didn't answer in time. (minimum 0) |
| `memPressureSome` | number | no | A microVM's memory pressure at `at`: the share of the 10 seconds before it in which at least one of its tasks was stalled waiting for memory (`some` avg10). Absent where the guest has no pressure figures. (minimum 0, maximum 1) |
| `memPressureFull` | number | no | As `memPressureSome`, for the share in which every task that wanted to run was stalled (`full` avg10). (minimum 0, maximum 1) |

### SandboxShape

The vCPUs and memory a sandbox asked for: the shape it was made with (a fork, its source's), and once its host places it, what it runs as. Known from the moment it's made, before its host says what it got (`resources`, with its disk). Absent: made by a named size and not yet placed, or made before shapes.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vcpus` | integer | yes | vCPUs: 0 for an isolate, which shares its account's VM's CPU. |
| `memoryMb` | integer | yes |  |

### SandboxShapeInput

What a new sandbox gets. A microVM restores a template snapshot on its host: by default the one its host keeps for its vCPU count, whatever its memory and disk, so a shape off the presets is as fast as a preset once that count's template is made. A host with shared templates turned off keeps one per preset, and a shape off the presets boots from scratch.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vcpus` | integer | no | A microVM's vCPUs. An isolate has none of its own: it shares its account's VM's CPU. (minimum 1) |
| `memoryMb` | integer | no | Memory in MB. An isolate takes 128 to 512 in steps of 64; a microVM up to what a host offers (`getSandboxShapes`). Needed unless `diskGb` is given alone. (minimum 128) |
| `diskGb` | integer | no | A microVM's disk in GB, chosen apart from its vCPUs and memory, within `getSandboxShapes`' `microvm.diskGb`. Alone (with `size` or neither), the vCPUs and memory are that size's or the default's. Default: the disk its host gives the shape. Not for an isolate, or with `from`: a sandbox made from a snapshot keeps the snapshot's disk. (minimum 1) |

### SandboxStartup

How its machine's latest start (a create, fork, start or resume) took its time, phase by phase, as its host measured it: a slow disk phase is a full copy of its disk, a slow boot or agent phase a busy host. microVMs only, and only from a host that reports it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `disk` | `"reflink"` or `"copy"` or `"move"` or `"new"` | no | How its disk was made: `reflink`, a clone of the snapshot's disk that shares its blocks (at once, on a host whose disk is XFS or btrfs); `copy`, a full copy of the snapshot's data (a host on ext4, which has no reflinks); `move`, a live fork's own snapshot's disk; `new`, an empty disk. Absent when it kept its own (a resume). |
| `diskMs` | number | yes | Making its disk, in milliseconds. |
| `snapshotMs` | number | no | For a fork of a running sandbox: the live snapshot of its source it was made from. |
| `bootMs` | number | yes | Its machine booted, or its snapshot loaded into it (a restore with memory), in milliseconds. |
| `agentMs` | number | yes | From then until its guest agent answered, in milliseconds: on a cold boot, the guest's kernel and init too. |
| `hostMs` | number | yes | The whole start on its host, in milliseconds: these phases and the rest (its network, identity and mounts). |
| `totalMs` | number | yes | From Kantel's call to its host until the host answered, in milliseconds. Well over `hostMs` is time on the way to and from the host, not on it. |

### SandboxState

`starting`: being placed and booted. `running`: commands run now. `stopping`: its disk is being saved. `stopped`: no machine; its disk is kept as its newest snapshot, and running programs are gone. `paused`: like `stopped`, but its memory is kept too, so `resume` carries on where it left off (microVMs only). `error`: the last operation failed or the machine was lost; `recover` or `resume` it. `deleting`, `deleted`: erased for good, with its snapshots.

One of: `"starting"` or `"running"` or `"stopping"` or `"stopped"` or `"paused"` or `"error"` or `"deleting"` or `"deleted"`.

### SandboxType

`isolate`: a V8 isolate running just-bash, a bash written in TypeScript, over files kept in `/workspace`. Starts in milliseconds and costs almost nothing. It has curl, jq, grep, rg, sed, awk and the usual text tools, and `node` (JavaScript and TypeScript, no npm packages) and `python` (Pyodide: the standard library and numpy, no pip install) where its `capabilities` say so (`javascript`, `python`), but no git, package manager or other program of its own, no Docker, desktop, ports or SSH. It can be upgraded to a microVM in place. `microvm`: a Firecracker microVM with a full Linux, root, Docker and `/dev/kvm` inside, a desktop, a browser and SSH.

One of: `"isolate"` or `"microvm"`.

### SandboxUsagePoint

One interval's means, and its highest CPU and memory. A sandbox keeps a day of 5-minute means and hourly ones for the six days before, so an interval within the day can be as fine as 5 minutes, and one before it is an hour's mean at best.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |
| `cpu` | number | yes | CPU utilisation over the interval. (minimum 0, maximum 1) |
| `memoryMb` | number | yes |  |
| `cpuMax` | number | no | The highest CPU reading in the interval, where `measured`. From a mean kept before peaks were, its mean. (minimum 0, maximum 1) |
| `memoryMbMax` | number | no | The most memory in use in one reading in the interval, where `measured`: a sandbox's peak can be twice its mean or more, so size it from this. From a mean kept before peaks were, its mean. |
| `runningSeconds` | number | yes |  |
| `cost` | number | yes |  |
| `measured` | boolean | no | Whether any kept reading covers the interval: false where there is none (stopped, or older than the week kept), and `cpu` and `memoryMb` are then 0 for want of a figure, not measured as 0. Absent from a gateway before it. |
| `diskUsedBytes` | integer | no | The sandbox's own disk in use, its mean over the interval; absent where its host doesn't send it. (minimum 0) |
| `ioPressure` | number | no | The share of the interval in which at least one of its tasks waited on IO, its mean; absent where its guest has no pressure figures. (minimum 0, maximum 1) |

`private`: only the person who made it (and API keys of theirs) may see or use it. `organisation`: every member of its organisation may. A personal account's sandboxes are always `private`.

### SnapshotKind

`automatic`: one of a sandbox's own history, taken as it runs and at each stop; the newest is what a resume or fork uses, and older ones expire. `saved`: kept under a name until deleted, and usable as a template for new sandboxes, even after its sandbox is deleted.

One of: `"automatic"` or `"saved"`.

### StickyDisk

A named, versioned disk, attached to microVMs at a path. Each sandbox gets its own copy-on-write copy of the newest version its host has (an empty disk at first), writes what it likes, and its writes go when it does unless it is committed: a commit makes that sandbox's copy the disk's next version. For caches that jobs warm and reuse, such as a pnpm store, Docker's images or a git mirror. Experimental.

| `description` | string | no |  |
| `sizeGb` | integer | yes | Each copy's size: what a sandbox can fill. |
| `head` | string | no | The newest committed version; absent until one is. |
| `versions` | [StickyDiskVersion](/api/reference/types/#stickydiskversion)[] | no | The newest 20, newest first, on a get. |
| `createdAt` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |
| `updatedAt` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |

### TemplateBase

The Kantel base image it boots: a channel the deployment publishes (`/v1/template-bases`), or a digest one published. Default: `kantel/sandbox`'s `stable` channel; until that channel publishes a digest, each host's own sandbox image.

One of: [TemplateBaseChannelRef](/api/reference/types/#templatebasechannelref) or [TemplateBasePinned](/api/reference/types/#templatebasepinned).

### TemplateBaseChannel

A base image's channel and the digests it has published.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | yes |  |
| `channel` | string | yes |  |
| `digest` | string | yes | The digest it publishes now. |
| `publishedAt` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |
| `history` | [TemplateBaseRelease](/api/reference/types/#templatebaserelease)[] | yes | Every digest it has published, newest first. |

### TemplateBaseChannelRef

Follow a channel: rebuilt when it publishes a new digest.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | yes | The base image, such as `kantel/sandbox`. (at most 255 characters) |
| `channel` | string | yes | A channel, such as `stable`. |

### TemplateBaseList

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | [TemplateBaseChannel](/api/reference/types/#templatebasechannel)[] | yes |  |

Pin an exact digest, one its channels published: never rebuilt for a new release.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | yes | The base image, such as `kantel/sandbox`. (at most 255 characters) |
| `digest` | string | yes | The digest pinned. |

### TemplateBaseRelease

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `digest` | string | yes |  |
| `publishedAt` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |

How far a pinned base is behind its channel.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `releases` | integer | yes | How many digests the base's channel has published since the pinned one. |
| `since` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |
| `latestDigest` | string | yes |  |

### TemplateBuildStatus

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `"none"` or `"building"` or `"ready"` or `"stale"` or `"failed"` | yes | `none`: nothing built yet; sandboxes boot fresh. `stale`: what is built is for an older key, and used until its replacement is ready if it is of the template's current version. A `ready` snapshot of an older version starts no sandbox: they boot fresh until the current version's is ready. A template with a Dockerfile or image reference doesn't boot fresh before its current version's image is built: its sandboxes wait for that build (`unavailable` until then). |
| `ready` | [TemplateSnapshot](/api/reference/types/#templatesnapshot) | no |  |
| `building` | [TemplateSnapshot](/api/reference/types/#templatesnapshot) | no |  |
| `error` | string | no |  |
| `behind` | [TemplateBehind](/api/reference/types/#templatebehind) | no |  |

### TemplateBuiltFrom

What a template snapshot was built from.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `baseImage` | string | yes |  |
| `channel` | string | no | The channel it followed; absent when pinned. |
| `baseDigest` | string | yes | Empty while the channel has no published digest. |
| `pinned` | boolean | yes |  |
| `imageDigest` | string | no | The digest of the image its host booted, as the host reported it: for an `image`, the digest the reference resolved to; for a `dockerfile`, the built image's ID. |
| `source` | `"kantel-base"` or `"dockerfile"` or `"image"` | no | The template image's kind it was built from. Absent: `kantel-base`. |
| `dockerfileDigest` | string | no | For a `dockerfile`, the SHA-256 of the Dockerfile built, `sha256:…`. |
| `imageRef` | string | no | For an `image`, the reference pulled. |
| `kernel` | string | yes |  |
| `firecracker` | string | yes |  |

### TemplateCacheKey

What a template snapshot is for: a change to any part builds another. A create starts from it only when it gets the same vCPUs and memory.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `templateVersion` | string | yes | `<templateId>@<version>`. |
| `baseDigest` | string | yes |  |
| `source` | string | no | A custom image's source: `dockerfile:sha256:…` (the Dockerfile's digest) or `image:<ref>`. Absent for `kantel-base`. |
| `imageDigest` | string | no | A custom image's digest: the one an `image` pins from the start, else the one its build made or resolved, recorded once the build answers. Absent for `kantel-base`. |
| `kernel` | string | yes |  |
| `firecracker` | string | yes |  |
| `vcpus` | integer | yes |  |
| `memoryMb` | integer | yes | With `vcpus`, the machine it was built as: the template's resources, which a fresh boot from it gets too. |

### TemplateDockerfileImage

Built in an isolated build microVM whose only way out is the sandbox egress proxy: its pulls, `RUN` steps and remote `ADD`s reach the template's egress grants and the registries the host's operator allows, and never a host, private or metadata address.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"dockerfile"` | yes |  |
| `dockerfile` | string | yes | A Dockerfile, built with no build context. `ARG KANTEL_BASE` then `FROM $KANTEL_BASE` starts from the template's `base`; any other `FROM` image is pulled. (at most 65536 characters) |

### TemplateImage

What a template's machines boot: `kantel-base`, Kantel's base image customised by the setup script; a `dockerfile`; or an `image` reference. Custom images are built only on hosts that build them in a build microVM. Default: `kantel-base`.

One of: [TemplateKantelBaseImage](/api/reference/types/#templatekantelbaseimage) or [TemplateDockerfileImage](/api/reference/types/#templatedockerfileimage) or [TemplateImageRef](/api/reference/types/#templateimageref).

### TemplateImageRef

Pulled in an isolated build microVM, as a Dockerfile's images are. The template's `base` isn't used. An image that isn't one of Kantel's boots through the guest agent the host injects.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"image"` | yes |  |
| `ref` | string | yes | An image reference, such as `python:3.13-slim` or `ghcr.io/acme/ci@sha256:…`. A tag is resolved when the template is built, and again on a rebuild. (at most 512 characters) |

### TemplateKantelBaseImage

The template's `base` itself, as its deployment publishes it; the setup script adds the rest.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `"kantel-base"` | yes |  |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | [Template](/api/reference/types/#template)[] | yes |  |

### TemplateSnapshot

A built template: its image booted once, its setup run, then snapshotted. A cache entry Kantel throws away and rebuilds at will, never one of the account's snapshots.

| `version` | integer | yes |  |
| `key` | [TemplateCacheKey](/api/reference/types/#templatecachekey) | yes |  |
| `keyHash` | string | yes | The SHA-256 hex of the key's canonical JSON. |
| `state` | [TemplateSnapshotState](/api/reference/types/#templatesnapshotstate) | yes |  |
| `hostId` | string | no | The host it was built on, which holds it. |
| `builtFrom` | [TemplateBuiltFrom](/api/reference/types/#templatebuiltfrom) | yes |  |
| `startedAt` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |
| `readyAt` | integer | no | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |
| `error` | string | no | Why the build failed. |
| `sizeBytes` | integer | no |  |

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

### TemplateSnapshotState

`stale`: built for a key no longer wanted, and used while its replacement builds only if it is of the template's current version. `failed`: not tried again until its key changes or the template is rebuilt. `discarded`: thrown away.

One of: `"queued"` or `"building"` or `"ready"` or `"stale"` or `"failed"` or `"discarded"`.

### Webhook

An HTTPS endpoint that gets an account's events, signed as Standard Webhooks are: `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` and the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `id.timestamp.body`, keyed by the secret after its `whsec_`). Failed deliveries are retried with backoff, up to 8 attempts.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | The webhook's ID, such as `whk_3m4n5b`. |
| `accountId` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `url` | string | yes |  |
| `events` | [EventType](/api/reference/types/#eventtype)[] | yes |  |
| `enabled` | boolean | yes |  |
| `createdAt` | integer | yes | Epoch milliseconds, UTC. |
| `lastDelivery` | [WebhookLastDelivery](/api/reference/types/#webhooklastdelivery) | no |  |
